chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: Slaughtering at Minā is for three days, so whoever wishes to fast must not fast until the three days have passed. And slaughtering in the towns is for one day, so whoever wishes to fast may fast from the following day.

key_terms.الصَّوْمَ: fasting, which is delayed until the nahr period ends
key_terms.النَّحْرُ: the ritual slaughter performed on the designated Eid days
key_terms.الْأَمْصَارِ: the towns or cities outside Minā
key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Minā, the hajj site where specific rulings apply
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ: a three-day period during which the ruling of nahr remains in effect at Minā
key_terms.مِنَ الْغَدِ: from the next day, meaning fasting may begin then
key_terms.يَوْمٌ: a single day, indicating the shorter nahr period outside Minā

ai.seo_question: When can a person begin fasting after the days of nahr in Minā and in other towns?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the days of nahr and when fasting may begin afterward. It distinguishes between Minā, where the period of slaughter extends for three days, and other towns, where it is one day, affecting the permissibility of fasting.
